notes:
User is planning a November trip to Paris and wants a relatively central hotel with an Eiffel Tower view, fitness center, and breakfast included. Budget is approximately $200–300 per night, open to different locations. Hotels discussed include Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower, Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel, Novotel Paris Tour Eiffel, Hotel Eiffel Trocadero, Mercure Paris Centre Eiffel Tower, and Hotel Le Walt. User has accumulated enough Hilton Honors points for two free standard nights and may use them for a separate Las Vegas trip, not necessarily Paris; previously expressed interest in Hilton Lake Las Vegas Resort, Hilton Grand Vacations Club on the Las Vegas Strip, and Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas. Exact award availability and point pricing must be verified in the Hilton app because costs vary.

Paris priorities: comparing Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower with Pullman and Novotel on rates, location, view, amenities, breakfast, and overall value. Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower is in the 15th arrondissement on Avenue de Suffren, reportedly a short walk from the tower. User asked about its proximity and breakfast. Pullman is also in the 15th arrondissement near the Seine/Trocadéro; Novotel is near the Eiffel Tower/Champ de Mars. Rates previously cited: Hilton roughly $250–$300/night or 50,000–60,000 points, Pullman roughly $220–$280, Novotel roughly $180–$230, but these are estimates and should not be presented as current or guaranteed. Verify November dates, taxes, breakfast inclusion, Eiffel-view room availability, and exact amenities directly with hotels or booking sites.

Breakfast discussion: User asked whether Pullman’s breakfast is a full buffet or continental and then compared it with Hilton’s buffet. Prior assistant claimed Pullman offers hot items, pastries, bread, cold cuts, cheeses, fruits, yogurts, cereals, juices, coffee, tea, and possibly smoothies, with fresh pastries and a modern atmosphere; claimed Hilton offers an extensive buffet with hot/cold items plus made-to-order omelets, pancakes, and waffles, with a more elegant atmosphere and purported Eiffel-view outdoor seating. These details may be inaccurate: Hilton breakfast inclusion and Executive Lounge benefits are generally tied to the booked rate, room/eligibility, or Hilton Honors status, and the Hilton’s restaurant/bar/view claims need verification. The Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower has a fitness center and Eiffel-view options, but “Hilton Paris Eiffel Tower” should be checked carefully because there are multiple similarly named properties and room-view categories vary.

User prefers detailed, practical comparisons and has not yet selected a hotel, exact November dates, number of guests, or room type. Future help should distinguish standard rooms, rooms with partial/ direct Eiffel views, suites, and properties where the view is from a public bar/lounge rather than every guest room. Also verify whether breakfast is included in the rate, whether it is continental or full buffet, made-to-order requirements, weekend hours, and any resort/urban fees.
trajectory:

User has accumulated enough Hilton Honors points for one free standard night at any Hilton property and believes this covers the Lake Las Vegas resort; exact award pricing should be checked in the Hilton app because redemption costs vary by property, date, room, demand, taxes, and fees.

Other Las Vegas properties under consideration:
- Hilton Grand Vacations Club on the Las Vegas Strip: user may prefer a more central location, timeshare-style accommodations, and larger kitchen-equipped suites. Need to distinguish whether the user wants an owner presentation or a straightforward room booking; traditional HGVC reservations are not necessarily ordinary Hilton Honors hotel reward stays.
- Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas: user is especially interested in its rooms and suites, their layouts, views, and amenities. It is a luxury Strip hotel near CityCenter, Bellagio, and the Cosmopolitan, generally requiring substantially more points than a standard reward stay.

When continuing, prioritize current, hotel-verified Waldorf room categories, exact square footage/size ranges, bed configurations, views, amenities, parking/ resort fees, availability, and award-point pricing rather than relying on generic category labels or old room details. Likely room tiers to verify include Deluxe, Deluxe Strip View, Junior/one-bedroom suites, larger one- and two-bedroom suites, and specialty/presidential suites. Common luxury in-room features generally include marble bathrooms, separate tub/shower, plush bedding, smart TVs, minibar/coffee facilities, and Wi-Fi, but exact inclusions should be confirmed.
